idiom_name: class ServiceProxy implements ServiceApi forwarding to the wrapped client
implementation_notes: TypeScript makes the equivalence obligation mechanical: class ServiceProxy implements ServiceApi fails to compile when a member is missing or its signature drifts, and the body forwards to the wrapped client with policy around the delegation, while callers keep importing the same interface type. The runtime forwarding stays ordinary code (or an ES Proxy object when the surface must be dynamic), and on the wire the framework forms are a Node-core reverse proxy or a framework interceptor; because types are erased, the compile-time guarantee must be paired with a runtime strategy such as delegation or a generated client.
pitfalls: implements is compile-time only: at runtime nothing is checked, so a proxy built by Object.create/spread or a generic Proxy can lose members without a type error.
Interfaces are erased, so a type-only interface cannot be reflected on - a Proxy trap cannot enumerate its members; decorators or runtime schemas are needed for that.
Forwarding must preserve async signatures: returning an unawaited or re-wrapped promise changes rejection timing and stack attribution for every caller.

variants.name: gRPC-js interceptor chain in front of the service
variants.idiom_name: grpc-js Interceptor registered on the server or channel
variants.implementation_notes: For a gRPC service the framework's interceptor API is the proxy: an interceptor receives the method descriptor, the call metadata, the options and the next call, so authentication, tenant checks, retries, tracing and error mapping wrap the service without touching it; grpc-js lets interceptors be attached to a server or to a channel, which is the same split as the JVM ServerInterceptor/ClientInterceptor. As with any interceptor mechanism, the chain applies to every method (unary and streaming) only if it is registered once for the server rather than per client instance.
pitfalls: Server-side and channel-side interceptors are separate registration points; configuring one leaves the other unprotected, and streaming methods need the same treatment as unary ones.
Metadata is the only per-call channel for identity and deadlines: state stored in the interceptor closure is shared by all calls and races under load.
Each interceptor must advance the chain exactly once with the expected metadata/listener shape; dropping or double-calling leaves the call hanging.
